parsed.why: No trans-specific offence or documented state campaign, but individual harassment is common, police sometimes misuse modesty charges against gender-nonconforming people, and the military-led state offers little documented recourse. Evidence on visitor-facing procedures and violence is thin.

The 2024 law criminalises gender-affirming procedures and same-sex relations with severe prison terms and deportation. Documented killings, targeting and official impunity compound the legal exposure; absent prosecution data do not mitigate it.

Anti-discrimination and hate-speech protections, comparatively liberal attitudes and prosecution of the Pride attacker are meaningful positives. Rising hate-crime reports, poor clearance and substantial underreporting show real hostility, but no documented visitor-facing restrictions or state targeting.

Constitutional and statutory protections are extensive, but reported widespread exclusion and weak investigation of anti-LGBT murders indicate limited practical recourse. No specific visitor-facing restriction or current pattern of state targeting is documented.

Gender-expression offences, official targeting of trans people, religious-enforcement raids and severe national criminal penalties create direct exposure. The 2025 raid detained foreign nationals and involved delayed release and public disclosure; tourist rarity does not offset these risks.
